description: This course, offered by the Department of Humanities & Social Sciences, enables students to understand economics principles applicable to engineering, learn the techniques of economic decision making, and familiarizes them with the basic fundamentals of the Indian financial economy.

syllabus.title: Introduction and Demand Analysis
syllabus.body: Principles of economics, how markets work: market forces of supply and demand, Elasticity and its application, Consumer equilibrium.

syllabus.title: Theory of Production, Cost and Firms
syllabus.body: Firms' production, cost and revenue behavior; resources optimization; Firms' behavior under competitive markets, monopoly, monopolistic competition and oligopoly.

syllabus.title: Engineering Economy
syllabus.body: Time value of money: Single-Payment and Uniform Series, Nominal and Effective Interest Rates, Evaluation Methods: Present Worth Analysis, Annual Worth Analysis, Rate of Return Analysis.

syllabus.title: Indian Economy
syllabus.body: Nature and size of Indian Economy, Problems - Poverty, Unemployment, Inflation, measures for controlling these problems, Monetary policy - meaning, objectives, tools, fiscal policy - meaning, objectives, tools.

outcomes: Understand the concepts of economics and use the principles of economics in the engineering discipline.
Develop insight into consumer and production behavior and the functioning of a market economy.
Learn the implications of monetary and fiscal policies in the Indian economy.
textbooks: N. Gregory Mankiw, Principles of Microeconomics
Krugman, Paul, and Robin Wells, Microeconomics, New York, NY
WG Sulliman, EM Wicks and CP Koelling, Engineering Economy, Pearson
Chan S Park, Fundamentals of Engineering Economics, Always Learning
Hal R. Varian, Intermediate Microeconomics, W. W. Norton and Company
Ruder Dutt and Sundaram, Indian Economy, S. Chand
